title: Pin Map Maker: Drop Pins, No Account
description: Use the Pin Map Maker to add markers for the places you care about — trips, stores, field sites — and share or export the map, no account needed. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a family planning a road trip drops nine pins from Denver to the Grand Canyon in two minutes — and the map that settles every 'how far apart are they?' argument is ready.
quick_answer: The Pin Map Maker lets you add markers for any places you care about — trip stops, stores, field sites, houses for sale — on one map, without an account. Click to drop pins, name them if you like, then share the view or export it for your document.

popular_table.note: Pins live in your browser and in the share link if you make one — there is no account and no server-side album of your maps. Keep the export if the map matters.

faq: How do I share my pin map?
Use the share link the tool offers — it encodes your pins so the recipient opens the same view. For documents, export a PNG with the Map PNG Export tool and embed the picture.
Can I move a pin after dropping it?
Yes — drag or delete and re-drop. Get positions right before sharing: recipients see the map as it was when the link was made, not your later edits.
No account tier counts pins; readability does. A few dozen labelled pins is a map; a few hundred is a dataset — that is CSV to Map's job.
Can I import an address list?
Paste-style import belongs to CSV to Map, which geocodes or plots coordinate lists. This maker is for hand-placed pins you choose one by one.
The basemap needs a connection to load; once you have built and exported the map, the PNG works anywhere, including a printed handout.
Can I colour-code pins by type?
Basic pins keep one clear style. When colour categories and a legend carry the meaning, build in Map with Legend instead.
What map do the pins sit on?
An open street map (OpenStreetMap data). If you share the picture, keeping the small attribution line is both polite and the licence's ask.
Eyeball clusters here; measure properly by drawing the line in the Map Drawer or running the pair through the distance tools — pins mark places, other tools price the gaps.
